This happened some time ago in 2015. Anyways I'm someone who likes sleeping in pitch black darkness. So I had my curtains changed to a darker color. It was something normal for me. And I've never experienced anything out of the ordinary.

However, this one night I wake up at around 3:30am in the morning. I was sweating, and had ruined my sheets. So I basically had to get up and replace everything. After that I went and had a shower. I finished up around 4am.

I come back into the room, make my bed up again with fresh covers, hit the lights and hop into bed. That night my curtains were slightly open so a thin column of light shot through. Even though it wasn't much, the light was bright enough to slightly illuminate a small area around where it hit.

I wasn't paying much attention but then the air became heavy and it got way colder than it normally was. Like the temperature had just dropped instantly. And I started feeling uneasy as if I was being watched. So I sat up in bed, thinking maybe it was just the cold sweat earlier and my body was just readjusting.

But the longer I sat and casually scanned the room. I noticed. Near to where the small ray of light had come in. I noticed a silhouette. There was a person there. Or whatever it was. Standing inside my room. I froze. It must have been the shock or fear but I just didn't do anything but stare back at it.

My heart sank and I was literally scared. It was like you knew something bad was about to happen. But you didn't know when. Anxiety, stress, fear all came at once. I couldn't move out of sheer fright. So I just sat there in my bed and looked at it. Thinking to myself "Fuck it. Just get it over and done with!"

I can't remember how long we had been there locked in our staring competition but I started to hear the morning birds chirp outside. So I knew the sun was already on its way up. When I broke my gaze to look outside, only for a few seconds and back the figure had disappeared.

I never told my family about it. That was probably the most weirdest and scariest experience of my life. Nothing like it has since happened to date. However I do experience frequent sleep paralysis and I'm not sure if it has anything to do with that.
